svg.title: A nurse is reviewing assessment findings for four clients with sensory disorders. Match each finding to the condition it best represents.
svg.desc: Cataracts cause a painless, gradual clouding of the lens with an absent red reflex and reduced night vision. Inner ear disorders such as Ménière's disease or labyrinthitis cause vertigo, tinnitus, nystagmus, and vomiting from vestibular dysfunction. Otitis media shows a bulging tympanic membrane with a diffuse or absent light reflex and fever. Open-angle glaucoma is typically asymptomatic early, then causes gradual peripheral vision loss with intraocular pressure of 22 to 32 mm Hg. AMD is not used because it causes distorted objects and central, not peripheral, vision loss, which does not match any vignette here.
